newsitem.title: UK: London gold slips to fresh recent low at fixing.
newsitem.headline: London gold slips to fresh recent low at fixing.

text.p: Gold weakened to its lowest fixing since January 9, 1995 on Tuesday afternoon as the market continued to react to a sharp sell-off in New York overnight, analysts said.
Bullion was fixed at $373.50, a dollar lower than the morning fixing, as sentiment towards the metal both in London and New York remained negative.

Some dealers said buying support could be expected at these levels but if the $372 price were breached -- which would take gold back to prices not seen since April 1994 -- then a further plunge was likely.

"I think it's going to stabilise around here in the short term. It should hold technically in the $372-$375 area," a London-based dealer said. On the New York Comex futures market, the key December delivery contract was trading $0.80 per ounce down on the previous close at $373.70 at the London gold fixing.
Market sentiment was largely bearish as investors shunned gold in favour of surging equities markets, and physical demand remained lower than expected.
Fears over the prospect of gold sales by miners and European central banks were also helping depress the price.
Gold was looking weak on historical price charts, and technical analysts predicted further losses.
"Selling pressure has increased, forcing prices clearly into new low ground and introducing our lower target of $372," said analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge.
Other analysts pegged gold's chief support level at $368-$370, the lows of mid-1994.
But in the near term the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday and Friday would discourage dealers from taking fresh positions this week, dealers said.
Silver followed gold lower to a fresh 20-month low of $4.70 an ounce before the price bounced back.
It was indicated at $4.75/$4.77 an ounce by 1520 GMT, down five cents from Monday's London close.
"It's really following on the coat tails of gold," a dealer said, pegging the near-term price band at $4.70-$4.80.
Platinum was also lower early but recovered to $378.50/$379.50, down $2.00. Palladium was at $114.50/$116.50, also $2.00 under the previous close.
